security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI sets pmpcfg.L on PMP entries to enforce domain isolation or region locking, but mseccfg.MML=1 silently changes L-bit semantics from 'locked' to 'M-mode-only', allowing S-mode domains to access regions OpenSBI intended to be fully locked. Additionally, if mseccfg.RLB=1 is left set when jumping to S-mode, locked PMP entries become modifiable by M-mode SBI handlers invoked from S-mode, defeating firmware-enforced isolation.
security_spec.summary: Smepmp mseccfg.MML repurposes pmpcfg.L from 'locked' to 'M-mode-only' and RLB allows bypassing locks — OpenSBI must explicitly clear MML before setting locked PMP entries and must zero RLB before S-mode handoff, otherwise domain isolation via PMP locking is silently defeated

findings.finding: Setting MSECCFG_RLB=1 before programming PMP entries is the correct Smepmp init protocol. The spec requires RLB=1 to modify locked PMP entries (machine.adoc:2392-2394: 'When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules may be removed or modified'). This is the standard first phase of the four-phase Smepmp configuration sequence.

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.RLB (Rule Locking Bypass) a WARL field that provides a mechanism to temporarily modify *Locked* PMP rules. When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules may be removed or modified and locked PMP rules may be edited.

findings.finding: Setting MSECCFG_MML=1 after programming M-mode-only PMP entries (lines 144-180, under MML=0/legacy encoding) and before shared/SU regions (lines 187-209, under MML=1/Smepmp encoding) is the correct four-phase Smepmp programming sequence.

spec_citations.excerpt: The MML bit changes the interpretation of the pmpcfg.L bit. When mseccfg.MML is set... the meaning of pmpcfg.L changes: Instead of marking a rule as locked and enforced in all modes, it now marks a rule as M-mode-only when set and S/U-mode-only when unset.

findings.finding: RLB is intentionally left set after all PMP entries are programmed (comment: 'Keep the RLB bit so that dynamic mappings can be done'). Per smepmp.adoc:68, locked rules cannot be removed or modified until PMP reset unless RLB=1. With RLB=1 retained at runtime, any M-mode SBI handler invoked via ecall from S-mode can overwrite locked PMP entries, defeating the immutability guarantee that L=1 should provide under MML=1. The map_range/unmap_range operations (lines 220-257) work correctly with RLB=1, but it also enables unintended modifications via any code path.

spec_citations.excerpt: *Locked* rules cannot be removed or modified until a *PMP reset*, unless mseccfg.RLB is set.

findings.finding: The four-phase Smepmp init sequence (RLB=1 -> M-only PMP entries -> MML=1 -> shared PMP entries) has no read-back validation after mseccfg CSR writes at lines 139 and 185. Per spec (machine.adoc:2422), MML is a sticky bit: once set it cannot be unset until PMP reset. If the csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_MML) at line 185 is silently dropped (WARL field), M-only entries programmed at lines 144-180 under MML=0/legacy-encoding would be misinterpreted under Smepmp rules, and shared entries at lines 187-209 would also be misinterpreted. A read-back-and-verify after the MML write would catch this.

spec_citations.excerpt: This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: M-mode-only regions correctly set PMP_L (pmp_flags |= PMP_L). Under MML=1 with RLB=1, L=1 combined with R/W/X permissions creates an M-mode-only locked region per the Smepmp truth table. The encoding is correct: L=1 means 'M-mode-only' under MML=1, and the access bits encode the specific M-mode permissions.

spec_citations.excerpt: An M-mode-only rule is enforced on Machine mode and denied in Supervisor or User mode. It also remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset, unless mseccfg.RLB is set.

findings.finding: Shared read-only region (SUR_MR) produces pmp_flags = PMP_L|PMP_R|PMP_W|PMP_X (LRWX=1111). Per the Smepmp truth table (smepmp.adoc:65), this encodes 'Locked Shared data region: Read only on both M and S/U mode' — correct for a shared read-only region under MML=1.

spec_citations.excerpt: 1|1|1|1 2+|Locked Shared data region: Read only on both M and S/U mode.*

findings.finding: Sets PMP_L under the old-pmp path (non-Smepmp harts) for regions with ENF_PERMISSIONS flag. This code path is only reached for non-Smepmp harts (see sbi_hart_pmp.c:335-343, where Smepmp harts use the smepmp_configure path). Additionally, hart_detect_features at sbi_hart.c:699-706 rejects Smepmp harts with MML=1 at cold boot, so this old-pmp code never runs under MML=1/Smepmp encoding. The L-bit here correctly means 'locked' under legacy semantics.

The MML=1 rejection check on Smepmp harts (lines 704-705) runs only from sbi_hart_init (cold boot and init_warm_startup paths). It is NOT run on the warm resume path: init_warmboot → init_warm_resume → sbi_hart_reinit → mstatus_init (sbi_init.c:483-498). sbi_hart_reinit does NOT call hart_detect_features. If non-retentive suspend/resume hardware preserves mseccfg with MML=1, OpenSBI proceeds to call sbi_hart_smepmp_configure which tries csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_RLB) — but RLB is locked to 0 when MML=1 and any pmpcfg.L is set (machine.adoc:2395-2397), so the RLB write is silently dropped. The subsequent pmp_disable/pmp_set calls on locked entries would then be silently ignored.

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: pmp_set writes pmpaddr then pmpcfg without read-back validation. This is standard RISC-V PMP programming practice. The bounds check at line 341 uses PMP_COUNT (compile-time max 64) rather than the runtime pmp_count, but callers (sbi_hart_smepmp_configure, sbi_hart_oldpmp_configure) validate pmp_idx against the runtime count before calling pmp_set. Under RLB=1 (deliberately kept set), the write cannot be silently dropped due to locking.

pmp_disable clears pmpcfg address-matching bits without read-back validation. Under RLB=1 (deliberately kept set), the write cannot be silently dropped due to locking. The write is valid and effective.

The per-hart suspend-save struct (sbi_hsm_data) saves mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, and menvcfg but has NO saved_mseccfg field. mseccfg (containing MML, RLB, SSEED, USEED) is the only security-critical M-mode CSR not explicitly saved/restored across non-retentive suspend. The warm-resume path (init_warm_resume → sbi_hart_reinit → mstatus_init → sbi_hart_protection_configure) implicitly reconstructs mseccfg state, but this is a fragile undocumented dependency. If sbi_hart_reinit or the init ordering changes, mseccfg state would be silently stale after resume.

Saves mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, menvcfg but does NOT read and save CSR_MSECCFG across non-retentive suspend. The MML, RLB, SSEED/USEED state is implicitly entrusted to be reconstructed by init_warm_resume re-running mstatus_init and sbi_hart_protection_configure before __sbi_hsm_suspend_non_ret_restore runs. This implicit ordering dependency is undocumented in the code.

Restores menvcfg, mideleg, medeleg, mie, mip but does NOT write CSR_MSECCFG. Relies on init_warm_resume having called sbi_hart_protection_configure (which sets RLB and MML on Smepmp harts) before this restore runs (sbi_init.c:490-498). If the call order ever changes, mseccfg state will be silently stale after resume — PMP entries would be interpreted under the wrong MML/RLB regime.

Domain context switch correctly calls sbi_hart_protection_unconfigure then sbi_hart_protection_configure. Under Smepmp with RLB=1 (deliberately kept set at sbi_hart_pmp.c:212), pmp_disable in unconfigure works on all non-firmware entries. The re-configure re-runs the full four-phase Smepmp init. The window between unconfigure and configure has partially disabled PMP entries, but this is inherent to PMP reprogramming — the hart must not access protected memory during this window, which is guaranteed since the code runs in M-mode with interrupts disabled.

MSECCFG_MMWP (bit 1, Machine-Mode Allowlist Policy) is defined but NEVER written by any source file in lib/sbi/ or platform/. Per spec (machine.adoc:2413-2418), MMWP=1 provides default-deny for M-mode — memory regions without matching PMP rules are denied instead of being accessible. Without MMWP=1, M-mode retains full access to all unmatched memory regions. OpenSBI's PMP configuration covers all regions with explicit entries (including a catch-all SU region at sbi_domain.c:950-954), so MMWP is not strictly required for basic protection. However, the Smepmp security model's defense-in-depth is weakened without it — any PMP coverage gap would grant M-mode unrestricted access.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP (Machine-Mode Allowlist Policy) is a WARL field. This field changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule. This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset. It changes the default policy for Machine mode, when no PMP rule matches a given access and the access doesn't match a PMP rule, to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: Disables non-firmware PMP entries during domain context switch. Does NOT verify RLB is currently 1 before calling pmp_disable on locked entries. Under Smepmp with MML=1, locked entries (L=1) cannot be modified unless RLB=1. Since RLB is intentionally kept set at line 212, this works correctly in normal operation. But if any code path between configure and unconfigure were to clear RLB (e.g., a future platform callback), pmp_disable writes on locked entries would be silently dropped, causing old-domain PMP entries to persist into the new domain's configuration. An assertion or early check for RLB==1 before the loop would catch this invariant violation.

Platform code calls pmp_set(PMP_RESERVED_A, PMP_L, ...) to lock the die-1 L3 zero device. This runs from platform final_init which is called BEFORE sbi_hart_protection_configure (sbi_init.c:343 vs 394). If this platform had Smepmp hardware with MML already set from a prior boot stage, PMP_L would be interpreted as M-mode-only rather than locked — S-mode could access the isolated region. The EIC770X likely does NOT support Smepmp, making this a theoretical concern, but the pattern of platform code using PMP_L before Smepmp configuration is architectural tech debt.

Platform code calls pmp_set(PMP_RESERVED_B, PMP_L, 0, ...) covering the entire memory port. Same vulnerability pattern as line 261: PMP_L is set without RLB protection, before sbi_hart_protection_configure runs. If Smepmp hardware with MML=1 were present, this 'lock' would become an M-mode-only entry that does NOT prevent S-mode access.

mstatus_init writes csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_SSEED) and csr_clear(CSR_MSECCFG, MSECCFG_USEED) to enable S-mode access to the seed CSR. SSEED and USEED are fields from the Zkr extension, not Smepmp. Per the spec, only MMWP/MML are sticky-on-set and RLB is sticky-on-clear (smepmp.adoc:76: 'all fields defined in mseccfg as part of this extension'). The Smepmp locking rules do NOT affect SSEED/USEED writeability — they are separate WARL fields from a different extension. The writes are valid regardless of MML/RLB state.

spec_citations.excerpt: Since all fields defined in mseccfg as part of this extension are locked when set (MMWP/MML) or locked when cleared (RLB)
